findings.text: The Item.js fix (`public/framework/core/Item/Item.js:25`) is correct but wider than the bug: every constructor field now goes through `set()`, so `new Page({title, icon, description})` runs `Page.set` three times before Page's own class fields exist, and leaves 3 fake lines in `page.jsonl_lines` and 3 "line" events. Checked in node: the title reads back correctly and Inbox.js:177 ignores those lines, so nothing breaks today. A simpler fix that avoids the side effects: after `assign()`, move each `fields` own property into `data` with `put()`.
Item.test.mjs only checks the fix on `Foo`, not on Page, the class the bug was found in (`Item.test.mjs:107`). One assertion on `new Page({title})` then `set({title})` would cover the real case.

The brief asks for each test to run through `node public/framework/core/Test/TestRunner.mjs <file>`. In the worktree, all three files report `0 total` that way, and the ready line doesn't mention it. The runner probably takes folders rather than files, so this is likely the runner's problem, not the tests'. Still, nobody has proved the tests run under it.
`List.test.mjs` fails only on `add([a, b])` (`got [null]`). The brief expects this until worktree/qf-5 merges, and the log says so. Re-run the test after that merge.

`Stream.test.mjs:13-17` stubs `location` and `Element` and registers its own loader for `/framework/` imports. Once qf-5's View guard and the shared site hooks merge, remove these stubs so the test doesn't keep a second copy of the loader.
`session.jsonl` has a ready line but no "complete" lines for the three subtasks, which the brief asked for, with pass counts. The pass counts are in the ready line instead.
